intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Noonan syndrome-like disorder with loose anagen hair-1 (NSLH1) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the SHOC2 gene.

checks.evidence_quote: We discovered that a SHOC2 mutation promoting N-myristoylation of its protein product causes Noonan-like syndrome with loose anagen hair.
checks.explanation: Causation by SHOC2 mutation is supported; heterozygosity is not explicitly stated (de novo germline missense).

paragraphs.text: Noonan syndrome-like disorder with loose anagen hair-1 is a RASopathy. Its facial features resemble those of Noonan syndrome, and it also has distinctive ectodermal abnormalities. Cordeddu et al. (2009) described the main features as reduced growth, often with proven growth hormone (GH) deficiency, cognitive deficits, distinctive hyperactive behavior, and hair anomalies. The hair is easily pluckable, sparse, thin, and slow growing, and loose anagen hair can be confirmed on microscopic examination. Most patients also have darkly pigmented skin with eczema or ichthyosis, cardiac anomalies (especially mitral valve dysplasia and septal defects), and a hypernasal voice (Cordeddu et al., 2009).

paragraphs.text: Tosti et al. (1991) reported a 4.5-year-old girl with loose anagen hair and Noonan syndrome. Her hair was short, blond, and easily pluckable, and it had never been cut. On trichogram, almost all of the anagen bulbs were abnormally shaped and lacked inner and outer root sheaths. A scalp biopsy showed marked cleft formation between fragmented inner root sheaths and irregularly shaped hair shafts.

paragraphs.text: Cordeddu et al. (2009) reviewed 25 patients with a SHOC2 mutation and found a fairly consistent phenotype. Facial features seemed typical of Noonan syndrome and included macrocephaly, high forehead, hypertelorism, palpebral ptosis, low-set and posteriorly rotated ears, a short webbed neck, and pectus anomalies. Patients had reduced growth, often with proven GH deficiency, as well as cognitive deficits. Most had distinctive hyperactive behavior that improved with age. Their hair was easily pluckable, sparse, thin, and slow growing. In 12 patients, loose anagen hair was confirmed by microscopic examination of pulled hairs. Most patients had darkly pigmented skin with eczema or ichthyosis. Most also had cardiac anomalies; mitral valve dysplasia and septal defects were significantly more common than in the general Noonan syndrome population. The voice was characteristically hypernasal. Referring pediatricians had thought that several of the patients had features suggestive of Costello syndrome or cardiofaciocutaneous syndrome as newborns or young infants.

paragraphs.text: Gripp et al. (2013) reported 5 unrelated males with the S2G mutation. Four of them had initially been suspected of having Costello syndrome. All 5 had skin hyperpigmentation, sparse light-colored hair, increased fine wrinkles, ligamentous laxity, and developmental delay. All 4 who were assessed had a structural cardiac anomaly. Four of the 5 had hypotonia and macrocephaly. Three had polyhydramnios, increased birth weight, or needed a feeding tube. None had been formally diagnosed with loose anagen hair. However, all had sparse, very slow-growing hair of unruly texture and unusually light color, together with unusually long eyelashes. On brain imaging, Gripp et al. (2013) found relative megalencephaly with enlarged subarachnoid spaces suggestive of benign external hydrocephalus. They also found a relatively small posterior fossa, shown by a vertical tentorium, and cerebellar tonsillar ectopia in 3 of 4 patients. One patient had periventricular nodular heterotopia, and a Chiari I malformation developed after birth. Another patient developed myelofibrosis at age 2 years without the JAK2 val617-to-phe mutation; he died at age 2.5 years after splenectomy in preparation for bone marrow transplant. This was the first hematologic neoplasm reported in a patient with a SHOC2 mutation. Individual patients also had pyloric stenosis, chronic lung disease, rectal prolapse, or severe behavior problems that required psychotropic medication.

They then sequenced SHOC2 in 96 patients with Noonan syndrome who had no mutation in known disease genes. In 4 unrelated sporadic patients, they found a heterozygous c.4A-G transition predicting a ser2-to-gly (S2G) substitution. In 3 of these patients the mutation was absent from the parents and paternity was confirmed, showing that it had arisen de novo. In a further cohort of 410 mutation-negative patients with Noonan syndrome or a related phenotype, they found the same mutation in 21 patients and showed that it was de novo in 12 families. No other disease-associated SHOC2 variant was found. The mutation introduces an N-myristoylation site. Unlike the wildtype protein, the mutant protein incorporated myristic acid, was targeted to the plasma membrane, and did not move into the nucleus after growth factor stimulation. In Neuro2A cells, expression of the mutant protein increased EGF-dependent ERK phosphorylation. When expressed in C. elegans, the mutant caused a neomorphic protruding vulva phenotype.

Using a RASopathy gene panel, they found a heterozygous c.519G-A transition in SHOC2, resulting in a met173-to-ile (M173I) substitution. The variant was not found in 6,500 asymptomatic individuals. The girl had inherited it from her father. He was tall and had intellectual disability, a high-arched palate, sparse hair, and clubbed nails. The proband had macrocephaly, ptosis, nystagmus, right optic nerve hypoplasia, and sparse, slow-growing hair that was not loose. She did not have short stature, a cardiac anomaly, hyperpigmentation, or loose anagen hair. In SHOC2-depleted cells, the mutant protein restored EGF-induced ERK1/2 activity to only about 10% above basal levels. It bound PP1c poorly and did not efficiently promote phosphorylation of RAF1 at ser338. Hannig et al. (2014) concluded that this was a loss-of-function variant and that SHOC2 mutations can cause a spectrum of RASopathy phenotypes.

checks.evidence_quote: Noonan syndrome due to a SHOC2 mutation presenting with fetal distress and fatal hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in a premature infant.
checks.explanation: The title, together with the abstract's male infant and p.Ser2Gly mutation, supports the claim.

checks.claim: The SHOC2 S2G mutation in the premature male infant with fatal hypertrophic cardiomyopathy reported by Hoban et al. (2012) was de novo.
checks.evidence_quote: detected the previously reported, pathogenic, de novo SHOC2 missense mutation predicting p.Ser2Gly.
checks.explanation: The abstract states the mutation was de novo.

paragraphs.text: Gripp et al. (2013) found the S2G mutation in 5 patients. One of them developed myelofibrosis, and others had structural brain anomalies.

checks.claim: Gripp et al. (2013) found the SHOC2 S2G mutation in 5 patients.
checks.evidence_quote: We report five patients with this mutation.

checks.claim: One of the 5 patients with the SHOC2 S2G mutation reported by Gripp et al. (2013) developed myelofibrosis.
checks.evidence_quote: We report on the first hematologic neoplasm, myelofibrosis, in a 2-year-old patient with SHOC2 mutation.

checks.claim: Some of the patients with the SHOC2 S2G mutation reported by Gripp et al. (2013) had structural brain anomalies.
checks.evidence_quote: In conclusion, we report structural brain abnormalities including benign external hydrocephalus, relative megalencephaly and small posterior fossa, postnatally developed Chiari 1 malformation and heterotopia with SHOC2 mutation.

paragraphs.text: In a 5-year-old girl and her father, Hannig et al. (2014) found a heterozygous c.519G-A transition in the SHOC2 gene, resulting in a met173-to-ile (M173I) substitution. Both had mild RASopathy features. The variant was not found in 6,500 asymptomatic individuals. In functional studies, the mutant protein bound PP1c poorly and was unable to fully restore EGF-induced ERK1/2 activation in cells depleted of SHOC2.

checks.claim: Hannig et al. (2014) found a c.519G-A transition in the SHOC2 gene in a 5-year-old girl and her father.
checks.evidence_quote: Both parents were tested, and our proband’s father had a heterozygous copy of the p.M173I variant.
checks.explanation: The variant was found in the 5-year-old proband and in her father.

checks.claim: The SHOC2 c.519G-A transition results in a met173-to-ile (M173I) substitution.
checks.evidence_quote: identified a novel heterozygous SHOC2 variant c.519G>A; p.M173I

checks.claim: The SHOC2 M173I variant was heterozygous in the 5-year-old girl and her father reported by Hannig et al. (2014).
checks.evidence_quote: identified a novel heterozygous SHOC2 variant c.519G>A; p.M173I.
checks.explanation: The father is also described as having a heterozygous copy, so both carriers are heterozygous.

checks.claim: The 5-year-old girl and her father carrying the SHOC2 M173I variant both had mild RASopathy features.
checks.evidence_quote: Our report of patients with mild Rasopathy symptoms caused by a novel SHOC2 mutation should improve the diagnostic accuracy
checks.explanation: Both are described as having mild symptoms; the father's features are described as very subtle.

checks.claim: The SHOC2 M173I variant was not found in 6,500 asymptomatic individuals.
checks.evidence_quote: This variant was not found in 6,500 asymptomatic individuals.

checks.claim: In functional studies, the SHOC2 M173I mutant protein bound PP1c poorly.
checks.evidence_quote: the GST-tagged M173I mutant of SHOC2 failed to precipitate endogenous PP1c effectively
checks.explanation: Shows that the mutant binds PP1c poorly.

checks.claim: The SHOC2 M173I mutant protein was unable to fully restore EGF-induced ERK1/2 activation in cells depleted of SHOC2.
checks.evidence_quote: This SHOC2 variant thus is unable to fully rescue ERK1/2 activity in cells depleted of endogenous SHOC2.

paragraphs.text: Motta et al. (2019) found a c.807_808delinsTT mutation in the SHOC2 gene, resulting in a gln269_his270delinsHisTyr change, in association with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy that began before birth. The mutant protein bound MRAS and PPP1CB more strongly than wildtype and increased MAPK signaling. It was not constitutively targeted to the plasma membrane.

checks.claim: Motta et al. (2019) found a c.807_808delinsTT mutation in the SHOC2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Here, we report on the third RASopathy-causing SHOC2 mutation (c.807_808delinsTT, p.Gln269_His270delinsHisTyr)

checks.claim: The SHOC2 c.807_808delinsTT mutation results in a gln269_his270delinsHisTyr change.

checks.claim: The SHOC2 c.807_808delinsTT (gln269_his270delinsHisTyr) mutation was associated with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy that began before birth.
checks.evidence_quote: which was found associated with prenatal-onset hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
